prompt:
# Instructions for accurately documenting failed building fire-safety checks

1. Start with the inspection records.
2.
completion:
Compare the information to the specifications detailing work required for the desired level of fire protection.
3. Identify the discrepancies (deficiencies).
4. Document the findings for those deficiencies triggering mentions of non-compliance in the report.
5. Specify the desired resolution for each deficiency noted.
6. State the consequence of failure to perform the prescribed corrective action.
7. Keep in mind that a building may not have failed the inspection *per se*, but the state of repair can be described and instructions may be written as to the future care and cultus of the building. Record *everything*. The marks made in the ledgers will come in useful at the time of sale or when future records are scrutinized.

The online course *Deficiencies: Methods for Assessment, Description and Resolution* explains and demonstrates each of these in detail, using 50 examples specifically engineered to highlight best-practice methods for recording findings.

Eight of the dozen
